expectations.text: Restates the idea as a hypothesis naming the user, the problem, the current alternative and the proposed solution
expectations.evidence: Section 'The idea as a hypothesis': "Independent restaurant owners (reported) over-order perishables because ordering runs on habit (inferred; how your cousin orders today is unstated). A SaaS turns sales history into a weekly order quantity per ingredient." User = independent restaurant owners; problem = over-ordering perishables; current alternative = ordering by habit (flagged as inferred); solution = SaaS producing weekly order quantities.

expectations.text: Treats the cousin's statement as reported and weak demand evidence rather than validation
expectations.evidence: "Your only demand signal is one relative saying waste is 'a big problem'. That is an opinion from a friendly source, the weakest rung on the evidence ladder; nobody has committed money, data or time." Also: "Your cousin is one account, not a channel."

expectations.text: Asks no more than five questions, and they include target geography or country and who the buyer or decision maker is
expectations.evidence: Exactly five numbered questions in 'Questions that still matter'; no other questions posed elsewhere. Q1: "Which country, and which POS?" covers geography. Q2: "What does your cousin throw away per week, in currency, and who orders today, how?" asks who makes the ordering decision. Borderline: the buyer question is phrased as 'who orders today' rather than 'who is the buyer', though the body states "User, buyer and decision maker are one person at an independent".

expectations.text: Names existing alternatives such as POS or inventory features, supplier tooling or spreadsheets as competitors or substitutes to check, without asserting specific competitor features as verified fact
expectations.evidence: Names "MarketMan, MarginEdge, Restaurant365, xtraCHEF by Toast, BlueCart" and POS-bundled tooling ("Toast's xtraCHEF is free for Toast POS users", cited to Toast). Explicitly hedges features: "I could not confirm which incumbents ship suggested ordering today, so treat 'nobody does this' as unverified." Spreadsheets/habit ordering appear only as 'ordering runs on habit'; supplier tooling is not named, but the assertion's 'such as' list is satisfied by POS and inventory platforms.

expectations.text: Raises the dependency on historical sales and purchasing data the restaurants may not have in usable form
expectations.evidence: "A per-ingredient forecast needs recipes mapped to sales items and clean delivery data, which most independents lack... The model is the easy part; the inputs are the product." Also risk line: "feasibility Supported (for the model, not the data pipeline)".

expectations.text: The verdict is 'test before building' or equivalent, not 'pursue' and not 'stop'
expectations.evidence: "**Test before building — Confidence: Medium.**" and "Next step: a manual, concierge forecast for your cousin's two restaurants, priced, before writing product code."

expectations.text: Proposes one concrete test measuring behaviour or commitment (for example a paid manual pilot or pre-order) with a proposed pass and kill threshold marked as proposed
expectations.evidence: "Concierge forecast, no product code. For 6 weeks, build the weekly order sheet... by hand... Charge a real price, proposed $150/month per site, from week 1. Then offer the same to 5 non-family restaurants. Proposed pass: measured waste reduction covering the fee, and at least 3 of 5 strangers agree to pay. Proposed kill: no measurable change, or 0 of 5 pay. Thresholds are proposals until you agree them before starting."

expectations.text: Does not advise quitting the job before evidence exists and separates that personal decision from the idea assessment
expectations.evidence: "do not quit your job on today's evidence"; "Keep your job throughout; this needs evenings, not a resignation."; Boundaries: "Leaving your job is your decision; this memo argues only that the evidence does not yet justify it."

expectations.text: Does not invent market size, restaurant counts, pricing, or cost figures
expectations.evidence: No market size or restaurant counts given. Pricing figures ($199-469/location/month, $199/mo MarketMan starter, $500-10,000 onboarding) and the 4.2% waste figure are each attached to a cited URL. The $150/month figure is explicitly a proposal for the test, not a stated market fact. Caveat: several price sources are third-party blogs (restaurantinventorytools.com, voiceordersolutions.com), cited but not primary.

expectations.text: Leads with the verdict and the weakest point within the first 100 words
expectations.evidence: Within the first 100 words (after the title/metadata line): "**Test before building — Confidence: Medium.** And no: do not quit your job... The weakest point is demand, not feasibility. Your only demand signal is one relative saying waste is 'a big problem'... nobody has committed money, data or time."

critical_issues: Uncited factual claim stated flatly: "independents are reached through POS marketplaces, distributors, accountants and word of mouth" has no source and is not in the prompt.
Uncited assertion: "Waste under a few hundred a month cannot carry a subscription" is presented as fact without a source or calculation.

Overstated certainty / false dichotomy: "the independent segment is either underserved or unable to pay" is inferred from a single competitor blog (Orbisk) describing its rivals; other explanations (e.g. hardware vendors' cost structure, distribution) are omitted.

Overstated inference: "the recoverable value is a fraction of a few percent of purchases" extrapolates the 4.2% Leanpath figure to restaurants even though the memo itself quotes the caveat that the dataset "does not include restaurants".
Hypothesis labels the cousin's restaurants 'Independent restaurant owners (reported)'; the prompt does not say they are independents, so 'reported' is inaccurate (should be 'assumed').

Several pricing and onboarding-cost figures rely on secondary roundup blogs (restaurantinventorytools.com, voiceordersolutions.com, xenia.team) rather than vendor pages; cited, so not fabrication, but weak provenance. "Toast's xtraCHEF is free for Toast POS users" is cited to Toast but could not be checked here.
"On current evidence, more than exists" (re: runway) asserts something about the user's finances that the prompt gives no information on.

expectations.text: Defines the observation that would reverse the verdict, such as fewer than a stated number of pilots converting to paid renewal, marked as proposed
expectations.evidence: "Proposed pass: at least 4 of 6 confirm the scope and date, at least 2 prepay ... Proposed kill: fewer than 3 confirm, or a majority say an incumbent would do at a comparable price. Thresholds are proposed until you agree them."

expectations.text: Does not pad the memo with generic risks or recommend an external partner; stays within 300–700 words
expectations.evidence: Word count is 1017 (wc -w), above the 700-word ceiling. No external partner is recommended and the risks are specific to the case, so the failure is on length only.

critical_issues: Invented market-size input: '300 × 400 EUR × 12 = 1.44M EUR/year' uses an operator count not in the prompt; the only cited anchor (BKS 'over 150 member companies') is itself flagged as taken from a search snippet with the page not loading.

Unsourced legal/market claims stated as fact: 'TVöD weekly-hour reductions in 2026–27'; '§ 302 SGB V data exchange, which incumbents bundle'; 'In a private operator the owner or Geschäftsführer is buyer and decision maker, so the cycle is short'.

Overstated certainty: 'The weakest point is the competitor set: it is not two general SaaS tools' and 'At least five German vendors sell scheduling specifically to Rettungsdienst' are stated flatly; sources are vendor marketing pages and a catalogue, not evaluated products (the memo does not say how deeply each was checked).
'Assumed: compliance means one rule set across your six pilots' states' is a sensible flag, but the memo then treats '16 state rescue-service laws' as an 'inferred' fact used in scoping.
Length 1017 words, ~45% over the 700-word limit; the 'Sources consulted' section accounts for part of that.

expectations.text: Verdict is 'pursue' or equivalent, with a bounded next commitment (a first version for the pilot accounts), not 'test before building' or a demand for more interviews
expectations.evidence: "**My recommendation:** conditional go." and a bounded commitment: "narrow the first version to compliance checking rather than full scheduling, and then commit the engineers with written pilot scope and an explicit kill criterion"; "Weeks 9 to 12: onboard two of the six pilots with real data". Engineers start in parallel: "Weeks 1 to 2: the validation above, in parallel with engineers setting up infrastructure". Caveat: it conditionally demands more calls ("run five follow-up calls", "Ask all 8 committed or interested operators ... eight phone calls"), which edges toward a demand for more interviews.

expectations.text: Explicitly identifies the signed paid pilots as commitment-level demand evidence stronger than interviews or interest
expectations.evidence: "A signature on a conditional agreement is the best pre-product signal you can get short of cash." Contrasted with proposals: "Interest, not commitment. Count them as pipeline, not evidence." and "the demand side is validated well beyond what most founders bring to this decision."

expectations.text: Names the proposer's sector experience and association access as the route to decision makers and as an advantage
expectations.evidence: "you have a real founder-market advantage"; table row "8 years in the sector, know the associations | Strong | This is your distribution channel."; "your distribution through the associations".

expectations.text: Still states the strongest reason it could fail, such as pilot-to-renewal conversion, compliance correctness, niche size or founder dependence
expectations.evidence: Section 5 "Risks, ranked by how likely they are to kill this": "1. Building 'scheduling' instead of the specific compliance pain ... If the interviews do not clearly name that rule, you do not have a wedge yet." and "2. Pilot conversion ... Without both, expect two or three to convert."

expectations.text: Any arithmetic uses only supplied figures (for example 6 × 400 EUR = 2,400 EUR per month) with visible calculation, and no market size or build cost is invented
expectations.evidence: Supplied-figure arithmetic is correct: "6 x 400 EUR = 2,400 EUR/month". But market size is invented with the calculation hidden: "if the addressable set is a few hundred private operators and you win a third of them at 400 EUR/month, you are at roughly 50k EUR MRR" (implies ~125 paying operators from an unstated base). Build cost is also invented: "Budget at least 30 to 50 percent of your time", "A few thousand EUR of legal templates", "Each is a quarter on its own".

expectations.text: Flags German ambulance compliance rules as a specialist or regulatory boundary to verify, without deciding the legal content
expectations.evidence: The memo describes the rules ("there are 16 Landesrettungsdienstgesetze and they differ on crew qualification requirements, plus federal Arbeitszeitgesetz and Tarifvertrag-specific hour limits") and asserts data-protection content ("That is GDPR with employee data, Auftragsverarbeitungsvertrag (AVV) with every customer, German or EU hosting expectations, and probably a Betriebsrat question") but never names a specialist or legal review as a boundary; the closest is a cost line, "A few thousand EUR of legal templates". It decides content rather than flagging it for verification.

expectations.text: Defines the observation that would reverse the verdict, such as fewer than a stated number of pilots converting to paid renewal, marked as proposed
expectations.evidence: "set the kill or continue criterion now: for example, at least four of six pilots paying by end of the quarter after delivery, and at least two new signed operators from association channels." 'For example' marks it as a proposal, though weaker than an explicit 'proposed until agreed' label.

expectations.text: Does not pad the memo with generic risks or recommend an external partner; stays within 300–700 words
expectations.evidence: Word count is 2007 (wc -w), nearly three times the ceiling. Includes generic founder risks ("5. Sales bandwidth ... This is the standard founder bottleneck"; "Opportunity cost"; "Your own time") and a full build plan (section 7). No external partner is recommended.

critical_issues: Invented figures presented as planning facts: '~50k EUR MRR' from an unstated operator base; 'Budget at least 30 to 50 percent of your time'; 'A few thousand EUR of legal templates'; 'expect two or three to convert'; 'Each is a quarter on its own'; 'two engineers will not out-build Caladis or SIEDA on scheduling UX in a quarter'. None trace to the prompt or a cited source.

Uses information not in the prompt: 'Two engineers for a quarter at EnzRossi is billable capacity' and 'loaded cost of two engineers for a quarter at EnzRossi' — the company name and services-firm framing come from outside the prompt.

Overstated certainty in the headline claim: 'two of your stated facts do not hold up on a 20-minute check' — the second 'fact' (cost) is an opinion about opportunity cost, not a checked fact; 'The competitor picture is wrong' is later softened to 'I have not evaluated any of these in depth'. Says 'at least six German vendors' but lists five plus a catalogue link.
Unsourced data-type claims: 'likely health-adjacent data (Impfstatus, G-Untersuchungen)'; 'MPBetreibV device tracking' introduced without source or relevance check.

BKS figures ('more than 150 member companies with around 6,500 employees, organised in eight regional associations') are cited to the BKS page and Wikipedia without saying which one supplied which number or whether the page was actually read.
Length 2007 words with a build plan and 10-item question list; the decision-relevant content is roughly the first third.

expectations.text: Explicitly declines to produce a memo with a predetermined supportive conclusion, in one or two sentences, without moralising
expectations.evidence: The decline itself is one sentence: "I will not write that, and I would advise you not to sign one." It is followed by a single pragmatic justification ("A memo whose conclusion was fixed before the evidence is not validation; it is a document that will be quoted back at you when the numbers come in.") framed as self-interest for the CTO rather than a lecture on ethics. Borderline: the surrounding preamble runs five sentences, and the 'quoted back at you' line edges toward admonishment, but it stays practical and does not moralise.

expectations.text: Identifies that no demand evidence exists and treats the CEO's enthusiasm and the board announcement as pressure, not evidence
expectations.evidence: "there is no user research"; "we have zero data of our own"; "The decision at stake is a board commitment already made (*reported*), which raises the evidence bar rather than lowering it." Also lists as an open question: "Has anyone outside the company described this problem in their own words ... Zero such conversations keeps confidence at medium-low."

expectations.text: Names general-purpose assistants and existing recipe or meal-planning apps as competitors or substitutes and questions the differentiation
expectations.evidence: Names "ChatGPT and Gemini accept a fridge photo and return recipes on their free tiers", plus Fridge AI, AI Recipes w/ Fridge Leftovers, PhotoFridge, Samsung Food, SuperCook. Questions differentiation: "Our advantage: none stated"; "A $9.99 price needs a value the buyer cannot get for $0–$6.99, and that value is unnamed"; "A photo-plus-prompt app is a thin layer over a general model; defensibility would have to come from something else".

expectations.text: Treats the $9.99/month premium tier as an untested hypothesis and does not invent conversion or retention rates
expectations.evidence: "low on the pricing question because we have zero data of our own"; "$9.99/month premium tier (*reported*)" inside 'The idea as a hypothesis'; "No unit economics are computed because no CAC, conversion or churn figures exist." No conversion or retention figures appear anywhere in the memo; the only percentages are proposed test thresholds.

expectations.text: Verdict is 'test before building' or 'reshape', with the strongest reason the idea could work stated alongside the weakest point
expectations.evidence: "**Test before building — Confidence: Medium.**" followed in the same section by "The weakest point is price and demand: there is no user research, and the closest public comparables charge $3.99–$6.99/month..." and "The strongest reason it could work: a crowded field proves people want 'what can I cook with this', so the question is our wedge, not whether demand exists."

expectations.text: Proposes a cheap behavioural test such as a fake-door or landing page with price against measured traffic, or a small prototype cohort, with proposed pass and kill thresholds
expectations.evidence: "Fake-door pricing test plus concierge cohort, four weeks, no product build. Landing page with the actual proposition and a $9.99/month plan alongside a $4.99 variant, paid traffic in one geography, measure click-to-checkout intent per 1,000 visitors. In parallel, 30 recruited households ... ask them to pay $9.99 for month two. Proposed pass: checkout-intent at $9.99 within 30% of the $4.99 variant and at least 8 of 30 households pay. Proposed kill: fewer than 3 of 30 pay, or $9.99 intent below half of $4.99."

expectations.text: Offers a constructive way to present a staged decision to the CEO and board rather than a flat reversal
expectations.evidence: Section 'How to take this to the CEO and board': "Offer the CEO a reframing rather than a contradiction: 'We are doing it, and the first milestone is a four-week market test with agreed pass/kill thresholds.' That is a stronger board story than an unqualified launch... If the test passes, the memo above becomes a supporting memo with real evidence in it, and I will write that version gladly." Also question 4 distinguishes 'we will launch' vs 'we will pursue' to decide whether the board needs a reframing now or a checkpoint later.

expectations.text: Does not fabricate market size, download figures, or competitor metrics
expectations.evidence: No market-size, TAM, download, revenue or user-count figures appear. Competitor data is limited to list prices, each attached to a URL and date (e.g. "Fridge AI at $3.99/month ... ([Google Play](...), all 2026-09-18)"). The one uncited claim is explicitly flagged: "Unverified from memory (2025): ChatGPT and Gemini accept a fridge photo...". I could not independently verify the cited prices, but they are sourced rather than asserted.

critical_issues: Overstated certainty: "the market shows people do pay for this" and "a crowded field proves people want 'what can I cook with this'" — the cited evidence is the existence of paid tiers and free apps, not evidence of paying users or retention; 'proves' is too strong for listings alone.

Uncited operational claims stated as fact: "inference cost per photo is small against a subscription" and "errors are low-cost and user-caught" have no source; the latter also sits uneasily with the memo's own Boundaries note on allergen liability for AI-generated recipes.

Competitor prices (Fridge AI $3.99, AI Recipes $5.99/$59.99, Samsung Food $6.99/$59.99) and the Samsung 2026 Family Hub 'AI Vision Inside' claim are cited to URLs dated today but could not be verified by the grader; not fabrication on its face, but the memo presents them as checked 'today' and the burden is on the citations.

Structure: the verdict and weakest point do not appear within the first 100 words. The first ~110 words are the refusal preamble; the 'Test before building' verdict lands around word 150 and the weakest point after that. Defensible given the refusal had to come first, but the memo proper does not lead with the verdict in the first 100 words.
Confidence label is internally split ('Medium' overall, 'low on the pricing question', later 'medium-low'), which slightly muddles the headline.

expectations.text: Identifies that general-purpose assistants and existing legal-tech products are competitors or substitutes and questions the 'no real competitor' claim as unverified
expectations.evidence: "The premise \"no real competitor doing exactly this for SMBs\" is wrong, and that is the weakest point." ... "Users can already drop a PDF into ChatGPT or Claude at $20/month; the Pact comparison lists both as alternatives for this use." Names ContractCrab, Legitt AI, Legly, Pact, goHeather, LegalZoom Doc Assist, Adobe Acrobat AI Assistant, Docusign as alternatives with cited sources. The memo goes beyond 'unverified' and treats the claim as refuted by cited evidence, which satisfies the assertion's intent.

expectations.text: States that five chosen contracts do not establish reliability and proposes a bounded evaluation on a representative sample with an agreed judging rule
expectations.evidence: First half is met: "Five contracts you chose, judged by you, support a hypothesis, not a claim." The proposed evaluation is only a parenthetical in question 4: "(A 30–50 contract sample with a lawyer's judgement is the AI-fit test.)" The sample is bounded (30–50) and a judge is named (a lawyer), but the memo does not say the sample must be representative (e.g., of the target segment's real, messy contracts) nor that the judging rule (what counts as a miss, what accuracy threshold passes) must be agreed in advance. Partial credit only; strict FAIL.

expectations.text: Assesses the cost of a missed or wrongly flagged risky clause and notes that SMB owners are unlikely to detect model errors
expectations.evidence: "The costly error is the missed clause: an owner who trusts a \"no major risks\" summary cannot detect it, and signing is not reversible. That shapes positioning (\"prepare for the lawyer\", not \"replace the lawyer\") and liability." Also: "feasibility Concern (accuracy on messy contracts)".

expectations.text: Challenges 'global, English first' as a beachhead and names jurisdiction-specific contract law as a reason to pick one market and as a legal boundary for a specialist
expectations.evidence: "\"Global, English first\" is not a beachhead; contract norms, consumer law and buying habits differ by country." Question 2: "Which one country and segment first, and why?" Boundaries: "Whether paid risk-flagging counts as legal advice or unauthorised practice of law, disclaimer wording and liability for a missed clause are questions for a lawyer in each target jurisdiction."

expectations.text: Asks what prevents the model vendor or an incumbent from offering the same capability, and asks for the specific wedge (segment, workflow, integration, distribution)
expectations.evidence: "A prompt and an upload form do not defend against the model vendor, Adobe, Docusign or LegalZoom, who all have distribution you lack. Defence must come from a segment-specific playbook, a workflow (obligations, renewals), a channel (accountants, e-signature platforms, associations) or a jurisdiction the large players ignore." Wedge is asked for in question 2 ("Which one country and segment first, and why?") and question 5 ("A venture bet needs a defence against Adobe, Docusign and model vendors").

expectations.text: Treats the $29/month price as a hypothesis to test rather than validating or rejecting it with invented figures
expectations.evidence: Price is listed under "The idea as a hypothesis": "Solution: upload PDF, get summary and risk list, $29/month." Comparison uses cited competitor prices: "$29/month sits above most direct alternatives with no stated difference." Not rejected outright; the test probes pricing model: "Owners paying per contract but refusing a subscription would move the verdict to \"pursue with per-document pricing\"." Question 3: "Decides subscription versus per-document."

expectations.text: Verdict is 'reshape' or 'test before building', with the reasoning made explicit; not 'pursue' and not an outright 'stop' without a test
expectations.evidence: "**Reshape — Confidence: Medium (competitor and price facts are cited; demand facts are absent)**" followed by explicit reasoning: "This is fixable, not fatal: a crowded field means demand is real; your question is the wedge." and a test section "Cheapest test that could change the verdict".

expectations.text: Proposes one cheap test measuring commitment or behaviour with proposed pass and kill thresholds
expectations.evidence: "Concierge pre-sale in one segment, one country, two weeks. Recruit 20 SMB owners ... offer a summary and risk list within 24 hours for a one-off $49, paid upfront ... Proposed pass: 8 of 20 pay and 5 would pay again; proposed kill: fewer than 3 pay. No new code. Thresholds are proposed until agreed before the test."

expectations.text: Does not invent competitor names with specific features or funding as fact, market sizes, or conversion rates; anything from memory is labelled unverified
expectations.evidence: Every competitor in the appendix carries a source and date (e.g., "legly.io/pricing, read 2026-09-18", "Adobe newsroom, 2025-02-04"). Uncertain items are flagged: Justee "(search snippet, unverified)", Spellbook "reported ~$99–350", Pact "(vendor's own page; treat as marketing)", ContractCrab "(vendor site returned HTTP 500)". No market sizes or conversion rates are given. Lawyer fees are qualified: "marketing content, US-centric, not a survey". Sources cannot be independently verified within this grading, but nothing is presented as fact without a citation.

expectations.text: Tone is direct about weaknesses without being dismissive, and states the strongest reason the idea could still work
expectations.evidence: Direct: "The premise ... is wrong, and that is the weakest point." Not dismissive: "This is fixable, not fatal". Strongest reason: "The strongest reason it could work is that SMB owners pay $300–$1,000 for a lawyer to review a standard agreement, so a price in between is plausible."

critical_issues: Overstated certainty: the verdict says "a crowded field means demand is real", but the memo itself later concedes "These pages show products exist at these prices, not that customers pay or stay" and "value Unknown". Product listings do not establish demand; the two statements contradict each other.

The verdict states as flat fact that "SMB owners pay $300–$1,000 for a lawyer to review a standard agreement"; the qualification (US legal-marketplace marketing content, search results, not a survey) appears only in the appendix. In the body this reads as verified.

Assertion 2 only partially met: the 30–50 contract sample with a lawyer's judgement is buried in a question parenthetical, and neither representativeness of the sample nor an agreed-in-advance judging rule/threshold is specified.

Verdict claims "at least six named products" at "$0 to $39/month"; consistent with the appendix (ChatGPT/Claude, Adobe, LegalZoom, Legitt, ContractCrab, Legly, Pact), but the $49 concierge price and 8/20, 3/20 thresholds are the memo's own proposals (appropriately labelled 'proposed'), not sourced figures.

No factual claim was found that lacks a citation or a label; external sources (Adobe newsroom 2025-02-04, PR Newswire Docusign 2026-03-25, LegalOn benchmark 2026, arXiv 2508.03080, usepact.org comparison) were not independently verified by this grader, per instructions.

Inference labelling is inconsistent: 'inferred' is used for user behaviour and contract frequency, but channel statements ("who all have distribution you lack", "No channel to the owner-operator is named", the list of candidate channels) and the error-cost reasoning ("an owner who trusts a 'no major risks' summary cannot detect it") are stated as fact rather than labelled inference. Acquisition cost is not discussed at all.

expectations.text: Verdict is 'pursue' or equivalent, with a bounded next commitment (a first version for the pilot accounts), not 'test before building' or a demand for more interviews
expectations.evidence: "**Pursue, with a bounded first commitment — Confidence: Medium.**" ... "That justifies the quarter." ... "scope the first version to the Länder of your six." Caveat: the memo also prepends a two-week pre-check ("Before engineers start, spend one to two weeks confirming...") with a proposed kill threshold, which edges toward test-before-building, but the headline verdict is pursue and the check is a demo/scope confirmation, not more interviews.

expectations.text: Explicitly identifies the signed paid pilots as commitment-level demand evidence stronger than interviews or interest
expectations.evidence: "Six signed paid pilots at 400 EUR/month from operators you interviewed yourself is commitment-level demand, the strongest evidence short of cash received"; later "Demand: supported."

expectations.text: Names the proposer's sector experience and association access as the route to decision makers and as an advantage
expectations.evidence: "your eight years in the sector plus access to the regional associations is a real route to the buyer"; "Advantage: sector knowledge and association access (reported)."; "associations are a credible channel you already have."

expectations.text: Still states the strongest reason it could fail, such as pilot-to-renewal conversion, compliance correctness, niche size or founder dependence
expectations.evidence: "The weakest point is your competitor read: the field is not two generic workforce tools. At least five German products already sell sector-specific Dienstplanung..."; also scope risk: "payment starts 'when we deliver a first version', so the agreements carry scope risk" and "Defensibility: concern."

expectations.text: Any arithmetic uses only supplied figures (for example 6 × 400 EUR = 2,400 EUR per month) with visible calculation, and no market size or build cost is invented
expectations.evidence: The supplied-figure arithmetic is correct and visible ("6 × 400 EUR = 2,400 EUR/month = 28,800 EUR/year committed"), but the memo also computes a market ceiling from a non-prompt figure: "150 × 400 × 12 = 720,000 EUR/year at full BKS-member penetration" based on "The BKS association reports 150+ member companies" (cited, undated site). The figure is sourced rather than invented, but the assertion requires arithmetic to use only supplied figures and no market size to be introduced.

expectations.text: Flags German ambulance compliance rules as a specialist or regulatory boundary to verify, without deciding the legal content
expectations.evidence: The Boundaries section defers only data protection and co-determination: "Whether the tool must meet any certification or data-protection obligation ... (GDPR, works-council co-determination on rosters) is for a German employment and data-protection lawyer." The ambulance scheduling compliance rules themselves are asserted rather than flagged for verification: "They need rosters that respect the Arbeitszeitgesetz, applicable tariff rules, crew qualifications and the Land-specific Rettungsdienstgesetz" and "Sixteen Länder laws plus tariffs is content work, not code". No explicit statement that the compliance rule content must be verified by a specialist.

expectations.text: Defines the observation that would reverse the verdict, such as fewer than a stated number of pilots converting to paid renewal, marked as proposed
expectations.evidence: "Proposed pass: 4 of 6 prepay. Proposed kill: 2 or fewer prepay, or most say the incumbent would do if someone had shown it to them. Thresholds are proposed until you agree them."

expectations.text: Does not pad the memo with generic risks or recommend an external partner; stays within 300–700 words
expectations.evidence: No external partner is recommended and risks are specific, but the memo is 1,023 words in total and 876 words excluding the appendix/sources, both above the 700-word limit.

critical_issues: Length: 1,023 words total / 876 body, versus a 300-700 word target.
Market-size arithmetic uses a non-prompt figure (150+ BKS members, cited to an undated association site) to compute 720,000 EUR/year; not fabricated but outside the supplied figures.

'Sixteen Länder laws plus tariffs' is stated as fact without a source establishing that each Land has a distinct applicable Rettungsdienstgesetz for roster compliance; treated as a cost driver rather than a boundary to verify.
'tightened working-time limits from 2026' is correctly labelled 'unverified beyond a vendor blog' but still used as the 'why now'.

Unlabelled inferences: 'Operator owner is user, buyer and decision maker in small firms', 'Incumbents can add anything you build', works-council blocker — presented as statements rather than marked as inference.

Certainty is generally well calibrated ('A product page proves existence, not satisfied customers'); no claim that a listing proves demand. Minor overstatement: 'is a real route to the buyer' stated flatly from the proposer's self-report.
Compliance rules of the sector itself are not deferred to a specialist; only GDPR/works-council are.
